verdicts.evidence: Dropping .sort() on categories makes territoryVocabulary return insertion order: rules --json --for emitted territories.categories as [background-work, scheduled-work, secret-boundary, configuration, schema-migration, port-adapter, startup, model-provider] instead of the code-unit order the source calls part of the byte-stable contract. The 848 unit tests, test/smoke.js, test/audit-corpus.js, test/spelling-conformance.js and check --strict all stayed green.

verdicts.evidence: Replacing [...categories] with [] empties the field: rules --json --for returned territories.categories = [] where the baseline listed 8 categories. On a mission carrying runward/territory.md, the same emptied set fed structurallyInertRows and both operator rows were then falsely reported inert ('no rule governs `background-work`, so this row can never surface one'), in JSON map.inert and in the printed footer. No layer went red.
